verdict.note: atomic replacement passed with server-only row ownership
Node 22 reviewSnapshot.test passed atomic Issues/Evals replacement; held stale publication fence is covered separately by graphCache.test.

Re-measured because this commit rewrote the snapshot's freshness contract: the published Issue half
now carries one content revision per issue store instead of the resident forge revision alone, with a
single comparator deciding whether a publication is new enough to answer.

The focused test plus the paired graph and paged-review source tests: 21/21 pass, 0 fail.
- reviewSnapshot.test.ts 2/2 — publication still replaces Issues and Evals as ONE atomic generation
  (no reader observes a mixed pair), and the new case pins the per-store invariant directly: a
  publication is current only when EVERY store reached what the read requires, so a forge lead cannot
  pay for a missed local write and neither can the reverse.
- graph.test.ts 5/5 — the graph summary still exposes counts only; the freshness stamp still moves for
  a thread write on either host and only for a thread write.
- reviews.test.ts 14/14 — the server snapshot still retains the row inputs pagination reads, revision
  is stable for one snapshot and changes with observable input.

Live cross-check through the real product, in the same session's pass run against the running
backend: a fresh local write is now readable on the very next GET /api/issues with no intervening
rebuild, and a close is reflected in the list immediately — the behaviour this contract is for.
